reason: A takes both viewports. At 1440px it pairs a gradient-branded 'Fleet Registry' header with a search bar, count-labelled language filter chips and a dense semantic table (status orbs, per-language colour dots, monospace numerals, release pills) that reads as a designed product; the bar's page is clean but generic, with incident cards carrying large amounts of dead pink space and a detached header nav. At 390px A reflows the table into aligned metadata cards with zero overflow, while B shows a clipped 'GitH...' nav link at the viewport edge. A's desktop/mobile consistency is deliberate and intact; B's strongest asset — the teal response-time area charts — only appears in two monitor rows and can't carry the page.
gap: No graphical data layer: add a small push-activity sparkline or uptime-style bar strip per repo row (or a summary stat band above the table) so the page isn't purely text/tabular — that's the one visual asset the bar has that ours lacks; also raise mobile filter-chip height to >=44px touch targets.
